description: Haemul Pajeon is a beloved Korean savory pancake, crispy on the outside and tender within, packed with a delightful assortment of fresh seafood and vibrant scallions. It's a perfect dish for sharing, often enjoyed as a comforting snack or a side dish with makgeolli, offering a burst of umami and fresh flavors with every bite. This recipe guides you to create an authentic and delicious Haemul Pajeon that will impress your family and friends.

ingredients.notes: shrimp, squid, mussels, clams, cut into bite-sized pieces

instructions.title: Prepare the Dipping Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds, and minced garlic. Stir well until sugar dissolves. Set aside.

instructions.title: Make the Batter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour and rice flour. Gradually add cold water (or anchovy broth) while whisking to prevent lumps. Add the egg and whisk until the batter is smooth. Do not overmix; a few small lumps are okay. The consistency should be similar to thin pancake batter.

instructions.title: Prepare Seafood and Vegetables
instructions.text: Thoroughly rinse and pat dry your assorted seafood. If using larger pieces, cut them into bite-sized portions. Prepare the scallions by washing and trimming them, then cutting them into 3-4 inch lengths. Thinly slice the onion and red chili (if using).

instructions.title: Cook the First Pancake
instructions.text: Heat a large non-stick skillet or cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Add about 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil. Once the oil is hot, pour about 1/2 cup of batter into the pan, spreading it slightly to form a thin, even layer.

instructions.title: Add Fillings and Finish Cooking
instructions.text: Quickly arrange about 1/4 of the seafood, scallions, and sliced onion evenly over the wet batter. Drizzle a little more batter over the toppings to help bind them. Cook for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Drizzle a tablespoon of oil around the edges.

instructions.title: Flip and Crisp the Other Side
instructions.text: Carefully flip the pancake using a large spatula. Press down gently to ensure even cooking. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until the second side is also golden brown and crispy, and the seafood is cooked through. If desired, you can briefly flip it back to recrisp the first side.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board and cut into wedges. Serve hot with the prepared dipping sauce. Repeat with the remaining batter and ingredients to make more pancakes.

tips: For an extra crispy pancake, use a combination of all-purpose flour and rice flour. You can also add a tablespoon of cornstarch to the batter.
Ensure your pan is very hot before pouring the batter to achieve a perfectly crispy exterior. Use enough oil; Korean pancakes are often shallow-fried.
Serve Haemul Pajeon immediately after cooking to enjoy its crispiness. It pairs wonderfully with a cold glass of makgeolli (Korean rice wine).
article:
## The Ultimate Guide to Haemul Pajeon: Korean Seafood Pancake Perfection

Imagine a rainy day, the gentle patter outside, and the comforting sizzle of a golden-brown pancake cooking on the stove. This quintessential Korean scene often features a beloved dish: Haemul Pajeon, the savory seafood and green onion pancake. More than just a meal, it's a culinary experience – a crispy, chewy, flavorful delight that captures the essence of Korean comfort food. Perfect as an appetizer, a side dish, or even a light meal, Haemul Pajeon is a versatile crowd-pleaser that’s surprisingly simple to make at home. Get ready to embark on a delicious journey to master this iconic Korean treat.

## What is Haemul Pajeon?

Haemul Pajeon (해물파전) literally translates to "seafood green onion pancake." At its heart, it's a traditional Korean savory pancake characterized by its generous inclusion of green onions (pa) and an assortment of fresh seafood (haemul), all bound together in a light, crispy batter. Unlike its thinner, crispier cousins like kimchi jeon, pajeon typically boasts a thicker, chewier interior while maintaining a wonderfully crisp exterior, especially when cooked correctly.

The charm of Haemul Pajeon lies in this textural contrast and the harmonious blend of flavors. The sweetness of the green onions, the briny freshness of the seafood, and the subtle savoriness of the batter create a balanced and deeply satisfying taste. It's often enjoyed with a tangy dipping sauce, enhancing its complex profile. Culturally, Haemul Pajeon is famously associated with rainy days, as the sizzling sound of the pancake on the pan is said to mimic the sound of falling rain, making it a perfect cozy indulgence, often paired with a refreshing glass of makgeolli (Korean rice wine).

## Ingredients You'll Need

Creating the perfect Haemul Pajeon starts with fresh, quality ingredients. Here's what you'll need to gather:

For the Pancake Batter:
*   1 cup all-purpose flour
*   1/4 cup rice flour (or potato starch for extra crispiness)
*   1 large egg
*   1 1/4 to 1 1/2 cups cold water (or cold anchovy broth for deeper flavor)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1/4 teaspoon black pepper

For the Seafood & Vegetables:
*   1 cup mixed seafood, cleaned and chopped into bite-sized pieces (e.g., shrimp, squid, mussels, scallops)
*   1 large bunch green onions (about 10-12 stalks), cut into 2-3 inch lengths
*   1/2 medium onion, thinly sliced
*   1/4 cup sliced red bell pepper (optional, for color and sweetness)
*   2-3 tablespoons vegetable oil (or any neutral cooking oil) for frying

For the Dipping Sauce:
*   2 tablespoons soy sauce
*   1 tablespoon white vinegar
*   1 teaspoon sesame oil
*   1 teaspoon toasted sesame seeds
*   1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean chili flakes, optional for a kick)
*   1 clove garlic, minced (optional)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Haemul Pajeon is straightforward. Follow these steps for a delicious result:

1.  **Prepare the Seafood and Vegetables:**
    *   Thoroughly clean your mixed seafood. If using frozen, thaw completely and pat dry to remove excess moisture. Chop larger pieces into bite-sized chunks.
    *   Wash green onions well. Cut them into 2-3 inch long pieces. For the aesthetic, you can leave some longer to arrange on top of the pancake.
    *   Thinly slice the onion and red bell pepper (if using).

2.  **Make the Batter:**
    *   In a large bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, rice flour (or potato starch), salt, and black pepper.
    *   In a separate small bowl, whisk the egg with the cold water (or broth).
    *   Gradually pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients, whisking until just combined. A few lumps are fine; do not overmix, as this can lead to a tough pancake. The batter should be slightly thick, similar to a thin pancake batter.

3.  **Combine Ingredients (Optional Pre-Mix):**
    *   You can gently fold the prepared seafood, most of the green onions, sliced onion, and bell pepper into the batter now. Alternatively, you can add them directly to the pan as you cook each pancake for a more rustic look.

4.  **Cook the Haemul Pajeon:**
    *   Heat a large non-stick pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Add 2-3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, ensuring the entire surface is coated. The oil should be shimmering hot.
    *   Pour about 1/2 to 3/4 cup of the batter (depending on your desired pancake size) into the hot pan, spreading it evenly to form a round pancake about 1/2 inch thick. If you didn't pre-mix, quickly arrange some green onions, seafood, and other vegetables on top of the batter in the pan.
    *   Reduce heat to medium. Cook for 4-6 minutes, or until the bottom is golden brown and crispy, and the edges appear set.
    *   Carefully flip the pancake using a large spatula. Add a little more oil around the edges if the pan looks dry. Cook for another 3-5 minutes on the second side until golden brown and cooked through. Gently press down on the pancake with your spatula occasionally to ensure even cooking and crispiness.
    *   Transfer the cooked Haemul Pajeon to a cutting board. Repeat with the remaining batter, adding more oil as needed for each pancake.

5.  **Prepare the Dipping Sauce:**
    *   While the pancakes are cooking, combine all the dipping sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Stir well. Taste and adjust to your preference.

## Tips for the Crispiest Haemul Pajeon

Achieving that perfect crisp exterior is key to an outstanding Haemul Pajeon. Here are some pro tips:

*   **Cold Batter is Best:** Use very cold water (or broth) for your batter. The temperature difference between the cold batter and hot oil contributes significantly to crispiness.
*   **Don't Overmix:** Overmixing develops gluten, leading to a chewy, not crispy, pancake. Mix just enough to combine the ingredients.
*   **The Right Flour Blend:** While all-purpose flour works, adding a bit of rice flour or potato starch makes a noticeable difference in achieving a super crispy texture.
*   **Plenty of Hot Oil:** Don't be shy with the oil. You need enough to "fry" the pancake, not just lightly grease the pan. Ensure the oil is hot before adding the batter.
*   **Non-Stick Pan:** A good quality non-stick pan is your best friend here, preventing sticking and ensuring easy flipping.
*   **Don't Overcrowd:** Cook one pancake at a time, or ensure there's enough space if cooking multiple smaller ones, so the pan temperature doesn't drop too much.
*   **Be Patient:** Let the first side cook thoroughly until deeply golden and crispy before flipping. Flipping too early will result in a soggy pancake.
*   **Press Down Gently:** After flipping, gently press the pancake with your spatula. This helps ensure even contact with the hot pan and promotes browning and crispiness.

## Serving Suggestions & Dipping Sauce

Haemul Pajeon is best enjoyed immediately, straight from the pan while it's still hot and crispy. Cut it into wedges or squares using a pizza cutter or knife, making it easy to share.

The accompanying dipping sauce is an essential part of the experience. The tangy, savory, and slightly spicy notes of the sauce perfectly complement the richness of the pancake. Serve the sauce in individual small bowls for dipping.

Beyond the dipping sauce, consider pairing your Haemul Pajeon with:
*   **Makgeolli (Korean Rice Wine):** The traditional pairing, especially on a rainy day.
*   **Soju:** Another popular Korean alcoholic beverage that cuts through the richness.
*   **Kimchi:** A side of fermented kimchi adds a refreshing, spicy contrast.
*   **Pickled Radish (Danmuji):** Its sweet and sour crunch provides a nice palate cleanser.

## Variations and Substitutions

While Haemul Pajeon is fantastic in its classic form, its versatility allows for many delicious variations:

*   **Seafood Selection:** Feel free to customize your seafood mix. Oysters, clams, or even imitation crab meat can be added. For a richer flavor, some recipes include a small amount of ground pork or beef alongside the seafood.
*   **Vegetable Additions:** Beyond green onions, sliced carrots, zucchini, mushrooms, or even a handful of spinach can be incorporated.
*   **Kimchi Pajeon:** For a spicy and tangy kick, add chopped kimchi (and a splash of its juice) to the batter. This is known as Kimchi Jeon, or if seafood is also included, Kimchi Haemul Pajeon.
*   **Meat Pajeon:** Skip the seafood entirely and make a beef or pork pajeon by adding thinly sliced or minced marinated meat to the batter.
*   **Vegetarian/Vegan Options:** For a vegetarian version, omit seafood and load up on mushrooms (shiitake, oyster, enoki), tofu, or an array of other vegetables. For vegan, ensure your batter is egg-free (use a flax egg or simply omit, adjusting liquid slightly).
*   **Gluten-Free:** Substitute the all-purpose flour with a gluten-free all-purpose blend, ensuring it contains a starch like rice flour or potato starch for crispiness.

Whichever way you choose to make it, Haemul Pajeon is a delightful journey into Korean cuisine. Its comforting warmth, satisfying crunch, and rich flavors make it a dish you'll want to revisit again and again. So grab your ingredients, fire up the pan, and enjoy the delicious art of making this iconic Korean seafood pancake!
